text:
$NMR traded 11.2 times its 7-day average volume in the last 24 hours. That is about 24.2M USDT, and it is the number I care about most here.

Price is 12.77, up 16% on the day and 32.6% on the week. But it reached 15.5 this week and now sits 17.6% below that high. Hourly RSI is 53, so the heat has already left the move.

This is not a market-wide push. $BTC is down 0.87% over the same 24 hours. Buyers came for this coin specifically.

My view: no trade yet. A spike on huge volume followed by a quick fade often leaves late buyers stuck near the top. The chart shows most of this week's gain came in one burst.

What would change my mind:
A move back above 15.5 with volume still far above average. Then the breakout is real and I turn bullish.
On the other side, a close below 12.36, the middle of the 7-day range (9.21 to 15.5), and I expect more of the gain to fade.

Sentiment sits in Greed at 73. In that mood I would rather wait for proof than chase.

Next I watch the volume on the next push up. If it holds, the move has support. If it dries up, the fade is the more likely path.

Decrypt reports that Bitcoin ETFs have now seen inflows for eight straight days, adding about $2.95B over 30 days as they bounced back from the Clarity Act sell-off.

That reads bullish. The $BTC price does not agree yet.

Price is 83,695, down 2.9% on the week and flat on the day at -0.17%. It sits 4.1% under the 7-day high of 87,279. Volume is at 0.8 times its 7-day average, so trading activity is below normal despite the headlines.

My read: the inflows are soaking up selling, not driving a move. That is support, but support is not a trend. Hourly RSI at 51 says momentum is neutral.

One more thing bothers me. Fear & Greed shows 73, Greed, while price is lower on the week. Sentiment is running ahead of the chart.

View: no trade yet.
Above 87,279 with volume back above average, the flows are finally showing up in price and I turn bullish.
Below 82,563, the 7-day low, the inflows are not enough and I expect more downside.

What I watch next: whether the inflow streak holds while price stays in this range, and which side of it breaks first.
